title: Worked Example 6
summary: Put Pythagoras into a quadratic equation, then solve it.
alt: Worked Example 6: A rectangle ABCD has sides (x + 7) m and x m and diagonal BD = (x + 9) m. Calculate the value of x.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A rectangular field **ABCD** has **AB = (x + 7) m**, **BC = x m** and diagonal **BD = (x + 9) m**. In **ΔBCD**, **∠C = 90°**. Find the value of **x**.

steps.title: Use the right-angled triangle BCD
steps.narration: The diagonal splits the rectangle into right-angled triangles. In **ΔBCD**, **∠C = 90°**, with **BD** the hypotenuse, **CD = AB = (x + 7)** and **BC = x**.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{BD^2} &= \role{legA}{CD^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ \role{hyp}{(x+9)^2} &= \role{legA}{(x+7)^2} + \role{legB}{x^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Expand each bracket
steps.narration: Multiply out the squares.\[\begin{aligned}x^2 + 18x + 81 &= (x^2 + 14x + 49) + x^2 \\ x^2 + 18x + 81 &= 2x^2 + 14x + 49\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Form a quadratic equation
steps.narration: Bring every term to one side so it equals zero.\[\begin{aligned}0 &= 2x^2 + 14x + 49 - x^2 - 18x - 81 \\ x^2 - 4x - 32 &= 0\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Factorise and solve
steps.narration: Factorise the quadratic, then read off the roots.\[\begin{aligned}(x + 4)(x - 8) &= 0 \\ x = -4 \;&\text{or}\; x = 8\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Choose the valid value
steps.narration: A length can't be negative, so reject **x = −4**.\[\begin{aligned}\therefore x = \role{ans}{8}\quad(\text{since } x > 0)\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

challenges.title: Which root?
challenges.prompt: The equation gives x = −4 or x = 8. Which value can x take here?
challenges.explain: A length must be positive, so x = 8. The root x = −4 is rejected.

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Why a quadratic?
notes.text: When the sides are given as expressions in x, Pythagoras' theorem becomes an **equation in x**. Expand, collect terms into `= 0`, then factorise.
